title: Canonical algebra structure map between compatible ring fibre products
statement: Let $A,A',B,D,C'$ be commutative rings with identity and let $b:B\to A$, $q:A'\to A$, $d:B\to D$ and $c:A'\to C'$ be unital ring homomorphisms. Put $P=A\otimes_B D$ and $Q=A\otimes_{A'}C'$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with their usual tensor-product ring structures and canonical $A$-algebra structures. Let $\varphi:P\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ be an $A$-algebra isomorphism. Put $R=B\times_A A'=\{(x,y):b(x)=q(y)\}$ and $E=D\times_Q C'=\{(z,w):\varphi(1\otimes z)=1\otimes w\}$, with coordinatewise ring operations. The canonical structure homomorphism $R\to E$ is $(x,y)\mapsto(d(x),c(y))$; equivalently it is the unique homomorphism whose two coordinate maps are $d$ and $c$ composed with the coordinate projections from $R$. No surjectivity hypothesis is needed to define this map, and zero rings are allowed.

source.place: Situation 08KH (situation-module-over-fibre-product) and Lemma 08KQ (lemma-properties-algebras-over-fibre-product), the structural map B prime to D prime in the opening construction. The pushout formulation defines this map even without surjectivity; when q is onto, Q canonically identifies with C prime / (ker q) C prime.

def structureMap
    {A A' B D C' : CommRingCat.{u}} (b : B ⟶ A) (q : A' ⟶ A)
    (d : B ⟶ D) (c : A' ⟶ C') (φ : pushout b d ≅ pushout q c)
    (hφ : pushout.inl b d ≫ φ.hom = pushout.inl q c) :
    pullback b q ⟶ pullback (pushout.inr b d ≫ φ.hom) (pushout.inr q c)
